clue.text: Upmarket — releasing one backside and pinching another, prone to wrinkles

indicators.note: pinching means gripping, so the remaining letters hold another piece inside them
releasing means letting go of a piece, so it is dropped from the word

parts.note: upmarket goods are classy, stylish and expensive
ass is American slang for the backside
another backside: rump, the hindquarters

explanation.surface: A cheeky account of a posh pickpocket letting go of one bottom to grab another, rounded off with talk of wrinkles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'releasing' leaves CLY; 'pinching' puts the other backside inside that, after the C. Both backsides are slang for the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crumply crumples easily, so it is liable to crease and wrinkle.

clue.text: Material impounded by evangelical iconoclast

indicators.note: impounded by means locked up inside, so the letters sit within the following words

explanation.surface: Some cloth seized by a zealous preacher who smashes religious images.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'evangelical' and the start of 'iconoclast'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calico is a plain cotton cloth, so it is a type of material or fabric.

clue.text: Throw aunties out? Not I!

indicators.note: out signals the letters of aunties being knocked out of order
Not I says the letter I is excluded from the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to throw their aunties out of the house and insists they themselves stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges AUNTIES and 'Not I' leaves out its I.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a rider is to dislodge them from the saddle, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Mathematical equipment on side of agricultural vehicle

parts.note: to be on the side of something is to be pro it, in favour
a tractor is the farm vehicle that pulls ploughs

explanation.surface: A piece of maths kit is attached to the side of a farm vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A protractor is the semicircular instrument used for measuring angles in geometry.

clue.text: Boor's gleeful exclamation

definitions.meaning: a coarse, brutish person, from the brutish creatures in Gulliver's Travels
a whoop of delight, a shout of joy

explanation.surface: A lout lets out a cry of joy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift's brutish humanoids gave English its word for a lout, and the same spelling is a whoop of glee.

clue.text: Lexicographer wearing underpants?

parts.note: long johns are warm underwear, shortened here to johns
if you are wearing a garment you have it on

explanation.surface: A dictionary compiler is pictured in his underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the long johns have lost their 'long'.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Johnson compiled the famous 1755 Dictionary of the English Language.

clue.text: Bird and elk embroiled in conflict with careless pedestrian

parts.note: the jay is a noisy member of the crow family

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the word for conflict

parts.note: war is armed conflict

indicators.note: embroiled means thrown into confusion, so the letters of elk are mixed up

explanation.surface: A bird and an elk are caught up in a fight with a heedless walker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embroiled' rearranges the elk and 'in' places the result inside the conflict, after its A.

clue.text: Try to pick up

definitions.meaning: a judge will try a case, that is, listen to it in court
to pick up a sound is to detect it with the ears

explanation.surface: An attempt to catch something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is the legal sense: a court tries, or listens to, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A court hears a case when it tries it, and the ears pick up sounds.

clue.text: Shaky armistice cut short by weapon

indicators.note: a shaky truce is unstable, so its letters are thrown into a new arrangement
cut short means the last letter of armistice is chopped off

explanation.surface: A wobbly truce is ended early by a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the final E of ARMISTICE; 'Shaky' rearranges ARMISTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a curved oriental sword, so it is a weapon.

clue.text: Ask again about port

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A request to repeat the question about a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Nagasaki is a major Japanese seaport on the island of Kyushu.

clue.text: Capture look capturing fool

indicators.note: capturing means holding prisoner, so the word for look encloses the fool

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
an ass is a silly person

explanation.surface: Seize a glance that has caught an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: To lasso an animal is to catch it with a looped rope, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Ink may run into crone's activity for sunny days

indicators.note: into places the scrambled letters inside the word for crone

parts.note: a crone is an old hag

indicators.note: ink that runs spreads and smudges, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Spilt ink trickles into an old woman's pastime for fine weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' turns INK MAY into AYMAKIN, which goes 'into' HAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Hay is cut and dried in sunshine; the saying is make hay while the sun shines.

clue.text: President's musical 21 mostly tinned

indicators.note: the 's stands for has: the can has, that is holds, the other pieces inside it

Hair is the 1960s rock musical

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: the answer to 21 across, a word for incubator

explanation.surface: A president's favourite show is the musical, mostly canned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tinned' really does double duty, supplying the container and implying the contents are inside it; 'mostly' drops the last letter of 21's answer, giving WOMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairwoman presides over a meeting, so she is its president.

clue.text: Temporary home of excavations

explanation.surface: Somewhere to stay while the dig goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British for lodgings, and plural of the archaeologist's dig.

clue.text: Sponger to dance, wearing jaunty fedora

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the anagram goes round the dance like a garment
jaunty means set at a rakish angle, so the letters of fedora are rearranged

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: A cadger goes dancing in a rakishly tilted hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jaunty' gives FOADER, and the dance sits inside it after the F.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeloader lives off others' generosity, much as a sponger does.

clue.text: Starting to catch a jerk stumbling into crevice? Splendid!

indicators.note: into places the jumbled letters and the opening letter inside the crevice

parts.note: a crack is a narrow opening or crevice

indicators.note: stumbling means tripping up, so the letters of a jerk tumble into a new order
Starting to means the opening letter of catch is taken

explanation.walkthrough: 'stumbling' makes KERJA; with the C from 'Starting to catch' it goes 'into' the crevice, before its final K.

clue.text: Voiceless, is in a phone company? That's like something out of Ionesco

definitions.text: That's like something out of Ionesco

indicators.note: in places the voiceless pieces inside A plus the phone company

parts.note: BT, British Telecom, is the UK's main phone company
in phonetics a surd sound is voiceless, like p or t

explanation.definitionFit: Ionesco was a leading dramatist of the Theatre of the Absurd, so anything resembling his work is absurdist.

clue.text: Meringue material, for instance, affected weight

parts.note: eg is short for exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters of weight are rearranged

explanation.surface: Meringue ingredients are said to affect your weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' turns WEIGHT into GWHITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Meringue is whipped albumen with sugar, so this is its main material.

clue.text: Musical genre for sweetheart on top of sergeant, say

indicators.note: on top of means the first piece sits above the second in this down answer

parts.note: an old flame is a former sweetheart
a sergeant is an example of an NCO, non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A girlfriend is perched on a sergeant, the musical type.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is the Spanish guitar, song and dance style from Andalusia.

clue.text: Head of government to OK thoroughfare stopping short of scaffold

indicators.note: Head of means the first letter of government is taken

parts.note: to OK something is to allow it

indicators.note: stopping short means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: a street is a public thoroughfare

explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping short' trims STREET to STREE.
explanation.definitionFit: The gibbet frame from which the condemned were hanged, a scaffold for execution.

clue.text: Composite picture of patriarch

definitions.meaning: an image made of many small tiles or pieces
relating to Moses, the Old Testament patriarch and lawgiver

explanation.surface: A collage-like image of an ancient patriarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mosaic law' is the law of Moses, the Hebrew patriarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An image built of tesserae, and the adjective for Moses, as in the law handed down on Sinai.

clue.text: Soldier, perhaps, under war god and despot

indicators.note: under means the first piece sits below the second in this down answer

parts.note: Tyr is the Norse god of war
a soldier ant is one type of ant

explanation.surface: A soldier serves a god of war and a dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldier is a soldier ant, not a human.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant is a cruel absolute ruler, which is what a despot is.

clue.text: Flash car carrying nothing back to incubator

indicators.note: back means the whole lot is read in the opposite direction
carrying means holding, so the car takes the zero inside

parts.note: a BMW is a showy, prestige car

clue.text: Looking up passages in love diary, month before: snoop around

parts.note: to pry is to snoop nosily

love means zero in tennis, written O
a log is a record kept day by day

clue.text: Rodent getting self-effacing cat half-cut

parts.note: coy means shy and self-effacing

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat

clue.text: High point of item carried over

clue.text: Harmlessness of Old Town hosting university pub, previously
